title: Holistic quality fence for canary and shadow traffic
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: We currently gate canary rollouts primarily on single-metric thresholds (delta on a representative score) and ad-hoc golden prompts, which misses regressions that manifest only under specific traffic slices (long prompts, function-calls, high-token responses) or under shadow/AB routing. Goal: implement a holistic 'quality fence' that evaluates candidate model variants across multiple sentinel prompt sets, traffic slices, and composite metrics, and connects directly to the rollout controller for automated pause/rollback and richer telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary controller can query composite quality score for a candidate and receive a pass/fail decision plus per-slice breakdown. 2) Shadow routing telemetry includes sentinel prompt success/failure tags and can be aggregated into scorecards. 3) Automated rollback triggers when composite score drops below configured baseline + delta for N consecutive intervals. 4) Playbook and dashboard created for manual override and incident postmortems.
approach: a) Define canonical sentinel sets (anchors) composed of: functional prompts, long-context prompts, safety-sensitive prompts, and customer-replay snippets. b) Calculate per-sentinel metrics: correctness F1/ROUGE where applicable, latency regressions, hallucination heuristics, and rerank delta. c) Synthesize a composite score using weighted percentiles with configurable weights per project. d) Implement a lightweight online evaluator that samples shadow and canary traffic (1-5% of requests) and runs deterministically hashed sentinel checks, storing results in rollup tables. e) Integrate with existing rollout orchestrator to support: immediate pause, staged rollback, or continue-with-monitoring. f) Provide dashboard and alerting for per-customer anchors and global scorecard anomalies.
implementation_notes: - Use existing eval pipeline components from ENG-41357 for offline scoring where possible. - For online checks, reuse inference sidecar to tag sentinel responses; keep sampling rate configurable per-customer. - Composite thresholds default to rolling-baseline (7d median) + absolute delta; allow explicit overrides for critical customers. - Ensure KV cache and batching behavior is mirrored between shadow and production routes to avoid false positives. - Add audit events for any auto-rollback decision so security/compliance can review.
rollback_policy: Auto-rollback if composite_quality_score <= baseline - 0.07 for 3 consecutive 5-minute windows OR if any safety-sensitive sentinel triggers a hard-fail. On auto-rollback: notify on-call, create incident draft with associated artifact links, and scale traffic back to last stable variant. Manual overrides require two approvers (PM + Eng SRE).
comments: 2026-02-19: Kickoff with Platform and SRE; agreed to prototype using a 2% shadow sample and a 5-min aggregation window.
2026-02-25: Design review - PM prefers per-customer anchors; agreed to allow project-scoped anchor sets configurable in Console.
2026-03-03: Security asked for audit trail for every auto-rollback; added explicit audit event requirement and link to compliance playbook.
2026-03-08: First prototype pushed to test cluster (pr: github.com/redwood-inference/rl-rollout/pull/174). Observed noise on very short prompts — adjusted weighting down for <16 token prompts.

2026-03-12: Engineering review with Observability team: added histogram bucketing for token-length slices and a new dashboard panel for per-tenant drift heatmaps. Next: wire alerting and complete runbook.
